A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LMask work. Their complete main texts and appendices provide readable equations, tables, figures and experimental descriptions sufficient for comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original TSPTW and TSPDL evaluations, ablations, generalization experiments and sampling-stability results in Section 5 and Appendix E.

after.justification: V2 retains original routing experiments and adds penalty sensitivity, backbone comparisons, decoding case studies and runtime evaluations.

M1.justification: Appendix B.1 removes violation-count penalties from the stated TSPTW and TSPDL losses, retaining penalties on violation magnitude. V2 also implements a ReLD backbone variant and tests scheduled penalties. The core LazyMask algorithm, RIE and default POMO architecture remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V2 adds two 19-node TSPDL instances for successful and difficult decoding case studies, extending the tested TSPDL size range. The main synthetic distributions, hardness levels, Dumas benchmark, time-window shifts and TSPTW-500 coverage are retained.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 add VSR-LKH and replace Greedy-L/Greedy-C with Random-L/Random-C, stochastic heuristics incorporating backtracking. This substantially revises the main comparison set. The original greedy heuristics remain in the TSPTW-500 comparison; OR-Tools' previously described TSPDL failures are now explicitly tabulated.

E3.justification: Table 5 changes the reported n=100 training instances per epoch from 10,000 to 100,000, without establishing whether this corrects documentation or reflects changed runs. Sampling expands from S=10 to S=3,10,30. New experiments introduce deeper-lookahead controls, penalty schedules, alternative backbone configurations and CPU-only timing.

E4.justification: V2 adds backtracking-versus-lookahead comparisons, penalty sensitivity, POMO-versus-ReLD analysis, two decoding/failure case studies and runtime analyses. Sampling-budget sensitivity is expanded. The existing entropy sweep, backtracking-budget study and 16-combination ablation are retained and reorganized, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: The ten-seed inference-stability analysis and its box-plot conventions are retained unchanged, moving from v1 Appendix E.6/Figure 5 to v2 Appendix E.9/Figure 8. No new uncertainty-estimation procedure or changed repeated-run count is reported.

E6.justification: Numerous results are added or revised. Table 1 changes PIP's hard TSPTW-50 gap from 1.12% to 0.18%; Table 3 changes LMask's n=20 benchmark infeasibility from 5% to 0% and gap from 3.9% to 0.7%. New comparator, sensitivity, backbone, sampling and runtime results substantially expand the evidence. These are revised reports, not established same-setting performance gains. The entropy study loses its objective and infeasibility entries when converted to a gap-only plot.

T1.justification: Appendix B.1 substantively revises the mathematical penalty definitions by deleting the indicator-based violation-count terms. The routing formulations, Gibbs-distribution framework, Proposition 4.1, Assumption 4.2, Theorem 4.3 and Appendix D proofs otherwise remain unchanged.

C1.justification: V2 removes the introduction's separate efficiency contribution claiming introduction of TSL and design of the penalty loss. It explicitly emphasizes entropy regularization and near-zero synthetic TSPTW infeasibility. The abstract and conclusion retain the central LazyMask/RIE, theoretical-guarantee and empirical-outperformance claims.

C2.justification: New Appendix E.4 explains efficiency through policy accuracy, error position and remaining search space, including a case that fails with 10,000 backtracks but succeeds with 11,000. Appendix F discusses hardware-comparison limitations and parallelization overhead, while penalty experiments add feasibility–quality interpretations. V1's specific warning about high-entropy training collapse is omitted.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit code-repository link, implementation details for new baselines, TSPDL lookahead explanations, penalty-schedule constants and execution optimizations. Conversely, it removes v1's disclosed training backtracking budget of 15 and exact PIP/PIP-D sampling batch sizes. Hardware and most architecture details are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references covering ReLD, neural k-opt, VSR-LKH and standard constrained optimization, and expands discussion of the already-cited DPDP. It explicitly identifies TSL with PIP's one-step preventative masking and acknowledges the established penalty technique, narrowing novelty toward backtracking and integration.

P1.justification: The overall introduction–method–theory–experiments structure remains, with focused novelty and training rewrites. Budget and entropy analyses move into the main text; detailed initialization and the 16-combination study move to appendices. Acknowledgments and an LLM-use statement are added, while broader impacts are removed.

P2.justification: V2 adds decoding heatmaps and penalty, backbone and runtime tables, and substantially expands the sampling tables. V1's budget plots become Figure 2(a–b) with a new comparison panel; its entropy table becomes Figure 4; the 16-combination heatmap moves to Appendix E.3. The conference template also changes typography and page layout.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens validation and applicability guidance through non-neural backtracking controls, failure-case analysis, sensitivity tests and CPU-only timing, while clarifying prior use of TSL. These gains are tempered by lost training-budget disclosure and inconsistent repeated medium TSPTW-50 results: the LMask gap is 1.68% in Table 1 but 1.73% in Table 10, which states that it repeats the main results.
